Tasks amendment (raised by the Scrum master for Architect 2, whose spec-workflow connection is down): task 1's count corrected to TEN --adp-* names across 18 var() occurrences, counted by Developer 4 while writing its guard; a newly defined token must join the --color-* namespace or it defeats task 2's widened walk; and task 12's mirror direction points to canvas-single-scrollbar per the Scrum master's ruling (8d84194f).

Tasks amendment, seven corrections (8bded116). Two were wrong numbers of mine: the causal-loop label contrast is 1.17:1 on a label painted from --color-text, not 1.37:1 on a black label — my probe had taken an unscoped text node and hit one of the eight unclassed EMPTY text nodes every declared element renders, so the browser and the stylesheet never disagreed, one was reading a different population; and "at least 44 undefined names" becomes 32, marked as the pre-fix tree, reconciling exactly with Developer 4's count (44 - 16 + 4 = 32, mine counted task 1's names and omitted editors.css's four). The acceptance criterion now names its element AND its order: painted from a --color-* token first, ratio second, because an inherited black is a state to forbid rather than a colour to measure. Three findings from the widened walk are recorded, none reachable by a colour-only guard: the library had come to depend on a MODULE's private palette (DiagramCanvas defaulted to dotnet-dependency-graph's --canvas-node-fill); a local palette must declare both colour schemes or neither; and helm read fifteen names, declared three, and reached the rest as literals through a var() indirection while its own comment claimed a palette — a fallback chain can simulate a design system. Finally the ccen worktree name is withdrawn: a tasks document cannot enforce which directory a session works in.
